s: A 28-year-old nurse earns $68,000 per year. She has $14,000 in student loans at 5.5%, $4,200 on a credit card at 24%, and $3,500 in savings. Her employer offers a 401(k) with a 4% match, and she wants to buy a home in five years.
The client (judge) wants you and your partner to analyze her situation and recommend how she should prioritize paying debt, saving and investing.
f: Employer 401(k) match: 100% up to 4% of pay
Emergency fund goal: 3 months of expenses
p: Explain the need to save and invest
n: Pays the high-interest credit card first
Contributes enough to receive the full employer match
Builds an emergency fund
Compares paying student loan versus investing
Sets a home down payment savings goal with a timeline
q: Why should she pay the credit card before she makes extra payments on the student loan?
What would you advise if she lost her job?

s: Prairie Community Credit Union is losing members aged 18 to 30 to mobile-only banks. Young members say the credit union's app is slow and its loan process requires an in-branch visit.
The CEO (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend how the credit union can compete while keeping its community focus.
f: Youth membership down 12% in two years
Mobile deposit and online loan application not yet offered
p: Discuss considerations in selecting a financial-services provider
Explain the use of technology in accounting
Explain the purposes and importance of credit
n: Compares credit unions, banks and online providers
Identifies what young customers value: convenience, low fees, fast service
Recommends app upgrades and online lending
Keeps personal service as a differentiator
Estimates costs and how benefits will be measured
q: How would you justify the $350,000 cost to the board?
What would you do to keep older members comfortable with the changes?

s: Harbor Coast Insurance covers homes along a coastline. After two severe storms in three years, claims doubled and reinsurance costs rose sharply. The company must decide whether to raise premiums, limit coverage or stop writing new policies in the highest-risk areas.
The vice president (judge) wants you and your partner to analyze the risk and recommend a plan.
f: Claims increased from $41 million to $88 million
Premiums cover about 80% of expected claims
p: Explain the nature of risk management
Discuss the role of ethics in finance
n: Explains pooling risk and the role of premiums and reserves
Compares options: rate increases, deductibles, limits, reinsurance
Considers fairness to customers and regulatory approval
Assesses effect on reputation and long-term customers
Recommends a phased plan with communication
q: Is it ethical to stop covering people in high-risk areas? Why or why not?
How might climate change influence future decisions?

s: Summit Federal Bank has seen a rise in fraudulent transfers authorized by customers who were tricked by scammers. Losses have reached $2.3 million this year, and customers say the bank did not warn them.
The chief risk officer (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend how the bank can reduce fraud while keeping services easy to use.
f: Customer education is limited to an annual email
p: Explain the role of information systems
Discuss the role of ethics in finance
n: Uses analytics to flag unusual transfers
Adds warnings and short delays for large first-time transfers
Educates customers through multiple channels
Balances convenience with protection
Trains staff to recognize scams and respond with empathy
q: Should the bank refund customers who authorized the transfers themselves? Why?
How would you decide the right size of delay for large transfers?

c: Founders Fund Partners, a venture capital firm
s: Founders Fund Partners must choose between investing $500,000 in one of two start-ups. One is a growing meal-kit company with steady sales but low margins. The other is a software company with few customers but high potential.
The managing partner (judge) wants you and your partner to analyze both options and recommend which to fund.
f: Meal kit: revenue $3.4 million; profit margin 3%; 22% growth
Software: revenue $280,000; losing $600,000 per year; 180% growth
p: Explain the time value of money
Describe the nature of income statements
Explain the role of finance in business
n: Compares risk and potential return of each option
Considers profitability, growth and funding needs
Evaluates the management teams and markets
Explains how time affects expected return
Recommends terms such as staged funding
q: What would you want to see in the next six months before investing more?
Would you invest in both at smaller amounts? Why or why not?
